standard_prerequisites.name: Noetherianity as the ascending chain condition on ideals
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Supplies the contradiction at the end of the counted proof (line 6446)
standard_prerequisites.use: Forbids the strictly increasing chain of kernels produced from a non-injective endomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: Iterated kernels of a non-injective endomorphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Built inside the counted proof at lines 6441-6445
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the chain of ideals whose strict increase contradicts Noetherianity.

core_obligations: Assume a surjective endomorphism f of R that is not injective, so that the kernel of f is a nonzero ideal (proof line 6441).
Form the chain of iterated kernels of f and observe that it is strictly increasing, since a non-injective endomorphism has strictly growing iterated kernels (proof lines 6441-6446).
Contradict the ascending chain condition on ideals of the Noetherian ring R, concluding that f is injective and hence an isomorphism (proof lines 6440-6447).
proof_roadmap: Argue by contradiction from a non-injective surjection and write down the chain of iterated kernels (proof lines 6441-6445).
Read the chain as an infinite strictly increasing sequence of ideals, which Noetherianity forbids (proof lines 6446-6447).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a surjective endomorphism of a Noetherian ring is automatically injective and therefore an isomorphism (statement lines 6435-6438). The proof does not use the module-theoretic statement that a surjective endomorphism of a finitely generated module is injective, nor Nakayama: it assumes a nonzero kernel and exhibits the chain of iterated kernels of f, which strictly increases, as a contradiction to the ascending chain condition (proof lines 6440-6447). The observation that a non-injective endomorphism has strictly growing iterated kernels is the step carrying the content, and the author writes the chain out explicitly. H2.
